issue_context.title: Optimize NodeVolumeLimits plugin
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

For pods that only use secrets and configmaps, this plugin adds some overhead at scale. @msau42  does this plugin need to run for those types of volumes at all? If not, we can add a PreFilter to evaluate if Filter can exit early.

### Why is this needed?

Improve performance at scale.

/sig scheduling
/sig storage
comments: @ahg-g I think I can help with this one after the discussion.
Yes, I think we can add a check for the volume types.
@tangwz do you want to work on this one?

> @tangwz do you want to work on this one?

/assign

Yes.

Hi, @ahg-g 
I understand correctly, we need add a `func PreFilter()` in `csi.go` and `non_csi.go`, then if we found pods that only use secrets and configmaps, we can exit before Filter.
This can be followed after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125, for pods don't use volumes, return `Skip` in prefilter, then we'll skip the Filter phase for the sake of performance.

> This can be followed after #114125, for pods don't use volumes, return `Skip` in prefilter, then we'll skip the Filter phase for the sake of performance.

Thanks, let me have a try.

> This can be followed after #114125, for pods don't use volumes, return `Skip` in prefilter, then we'll skip the Filter phase for the sake of performance.

So I should do it locally and then wait for the PR merged before submitting?
Yes, or you can wait until that PR is merged

@tangwz FYI: I created ☔  issue for the `Skip` status in PreFilter: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114399
Allow me to mention you there. Also, if you get interested in some other plugins' optimization, please feel free to comment on the issue by the way :)
#114125 merged, so you can work on this now.
@tangwz Do you still want to work on this one? I can take over this issue if you don't have enough time.

Get. I will do it.

review_comments: shouldn't we check that the PVC passes `matchProvisioner`?

> shouldn't we check that the PVC passes `matchProvisioner`?

I think `vol.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil || vol.Ephemeral != nil` has already include `matchProvisioner`, should we check more?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5ede346fc8c1558e4d3e67aa0d96da68eb1f727e/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodevolumelimits/non_csi.go#L308-L325

> shouldn't we check that the PVC passes `matchProvisioner`?

Yes and no.

I think the current state is correct: if the condition "ok || vol.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil || vol.Ephemeral != nil" is true, this mean that filterVolumes **may** include a given volume in a "filteredVolumes" set so we cannot short cut. If all volumes are not matching the condition, then we know that for sure filteredVolumes will return empty result.

More specifically if vol.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil, but NOT `pl.matchProvisioner`, we will not return Skip in PreFilter and in Filter we will not add element in filterVolumes, which is correct, but is a potential waste of time.

Is it feasible actually here to run filterVolumes directly and:
* store result in plugin's state so that we won't recompute this in context of all nodes (may save some CPU)
* short cut (return Skip) if we have an empty result?

This way we both save CPU and reduce risk of inaccuracy between PreFilter conditions and actual filterVolumes implementation.

Performance-wise I think it should be similar:
* if all volumes are not meeting "ok || vol.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil || vol.Ephemeral != nil" condition, we will just "continue" them in filterVolumes
This can be a separate PR for performance as we did for other plugins in PreFilter. wdyt?
Sounds good. Let's leave it for a follow up.

> Sounds good. Let's leave it for a follow up.

Thanks, I'd like to follow up.
For followup, if you want to take it: use `cmp.Diff`
also refactor these to `cmp.Diff` in a follow up.
